title: Steffel -ameke/-ame/-ami source audit v1
primary_source: Matthäus Steffel, Tarahumarisches Wörterbuch, 1809 scan/OCR supplied to the project
critical_control: William L. Merrill et al., El Diccionario Tarahumara–Alemán de Matthäus Steffel, Universidad de Sonora, 2020

locator_method.description: Case-insensitive token sweep over the supplied OCR TXT. Tokens were continuous alphabetic strings; the counts are locators, not lexical or morphological counts.
locator_method.warning: OCR noise, German words, lexical homographs, split forms and duplicate dictionary sections make these counts unsuitable as lexical frequencies. Every linguistic claim requires source control.

source_controlled_findings.steffel_metalinguistic_statement: Steffel explicitly describes ameke as the present active participial ending and states that speakers frequently omit/swallow final ke in pronunciation.

historical_surface_ameke_ame_pairs.note: Merrill explicitly notes the absence of final -ke in the appendix form

source_controlled_findings.ami_negative_control: Raw OCR strings ending in ami include lexical or otherwise unrelated forms such as Ami 'lose', pamí 'year' and guamí 'there'. No direct historical participial -ami token was recovered in the controlled Steffel sweep.

li_ameke_substring_audit.decision: supports expected accent/shape of tsanelíameke but is not an independent second root
li_ameke_substring_audit.analysis: contains the already controlled tsanelíameke family
paradigm tschutschá 'ungir' / tschutschelíla 'unción' / tschutschelíameke 'ungido'; Merrill cross-references it directly in the explicit discussion of tsanelíameke
li_ameke_substring_audit.caution: no morpheme-by-morpheme parse of tschutschelíameke was recovered

li_ameke_substring_audit.analysis: recurrent family with ganiléliki, ganiléruje and ganilíle
li_ameke_substring_audit.caution: the internal status/function of li cannot be assigned from surface form

li_ameke_substring_audit.analysis: Merrill derives the adjective from the lexical verb uilí; li belongs to the root
Merrill explicitly derives selíameke from the verb selí 'govern'; the relevant structure is selí + -ameke

adjudication.historical_li_plus_ameke_bridge: D1 confirmed by tsanelíameke; D2 independently strengthened by tschutschelíameke; no second full direct parse recovered

next_step: Search targeted historical and modern interlinear/grammatical sources for a second independent D1 parse of X-li-ame(ke); treat ganelíameke as a candidate for dedicated morphological analysis rather than promoting it from spelling alone.
